reasoning_traces.think:
The core methodology hinges on detecting active game moments through player kinematics—specifically, position and velocity data collected at 50 Hz. These data are processed using a thresholding mechanism on average court position (avg_pos_x(t)) to classify periods as offensive (>4 cm), defensive (< -4 cm), or transitional (within [-4, 4] cm). This binary classification leverages a tuning strategy akin to ROC curves, where ground-truth annotations from video data guide optimal threshold selection. The derived kernel maps these thresholds into a structured game state model, enabling automated identification of offensive and defensive phases. A secondary layer tracks possession transitions via ordinal increments tied to state changes, integrating spatial dynamics with temporal logic. The failure mode arises when thresholds fail to reflect nuanced gameplay or when positional ambiguity leads to misclassification during transitions. Dualities emerge between spatial and temporal resolution, where high-frequency sampling enhances precision but introduces computational overhead. Strategic implications include real-time tactical adjustments based on inferred game states.
